content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. Type checking passes on it. I couldn't compare sizes or results against the original, because `lodash` isn't installed and the original `src/module.ts` no longer builds.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 268 bytes (min+gzip) and 101 bytes of own code. I didn't run the original through the old lodash path, so I haven't checked the own-code allowance.

I read the installed es-toolkit 1.53.2 declarations and sources for each function:

- **`pick`:** now imported from `es-toolkit/object`. It takes an array of keys and copies only the keys the object owns, so `pick(row, ['id', 'name'])` works unchanged.
- **`sumBy`:** now imported from `es-toolkit/math`. The main version only accepts a function, not a property name like lodash's `'age'`, so the call became `sumBy(rows, (row) => row.age)`. That is the small adapter the brief allows. An empty array gives `0`, as before.
- **`toNumber`:** only exists in `es-toolkit/compat`, so I import it from there. It is `Number(value)` plus a `NaN` for symbols. `es-toolkit/compat/util/toNumber` doesn't resolve for either esbuild or tsc, so the file uses the `es-toolkit/compat` entry point.

I ran the compat `toNumber` on sample strings in the input range, such as `"92858+99"`, `".72e"`, `" 12 "`, `"0x1"`, `"-0x1"`, `"+.5"` and `""`. It returned `NaN`, `NaN`, `12`, `1`, `NaN`, `0.5` and `0`.

I did not run those strings through lodash's `toNumber`, so that matching is unconfirmed. From memory, lodash trims whitespace, rejects signed hex like `"-0x1"` and parses binary and octal prefixes, none of which can appear in the input range. The `"0x1"` case has no sign, so lodash falls through to a plain numeric conversion and should also give `1`. I didn't run any of the other exported functions against the original.

Switching `pick` and `sumBy` to the main `es-toolkit` import gives 267 bytes instead of 268, so I kept the subpath imports.
